Maintenance Report — MNT-0140-006

Asset: WELL-0140 (NE-07 Well 140, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 30 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 15 Aug 2023 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 391 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0140-0041 on 2023-07-27 Report written: 17 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0140-0041 showed the wellhead at 42.8 °C with the air at 39.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0140-017

Asset: WELL-0140 (NE-07 Well 140, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 18 Jul 2025 08:00 · Finished: 05 Aug 2025 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 442 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0140-0142 on 2025-07-17 Report written: 06 Aug 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0140-0142 showed the wellhead at 39.3 °C with the air at 35.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0140-017 (WS-06).
